extracted.intended_audience: reviewers of NIH research grant applications (NIH peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing critiques and assigning scores for NIH research grant applications, describing what to address in Overall Impact, each scored criterion, and additional/non-scored considerations (human subjects, animals, biohazards, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: General guidance for critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid general comments and provide specific details; provide sufficient context to orient your comments (e.g., does the comment refer to a specific aim?); make sure bullets have evaluative statements that indicate your assessment of a particular aspect of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the text within each scored section is consistent with the score. Address all relevant review criteria and critique sections (e.g., many applications require evaluation of issues in addition to Overall Impact, Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, and Environment). Include attention to Rigor and Transparency in research (rigor of prior research, scientific rigor, consideration of biological variables including sex, and biological/chemical resource authentication), as appropriate for the research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring consistency & support
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores must be supported by the content of the critique and the balance of strengths/weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores of 1-3 should be supported by clearly articulated strengths. Scores of 4-6 may have a balance of strengths and weaknesses. Scores of 7-9 should be supported by clearly articulated weaknesses (or lack of strengths). Prioritize strengths/weaknesses (state if a concern is major/score-driving or minor) otherwise concerns will be assumed to be of equal weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess likelihood the research will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a paragraph supporting the overall impact score that: introduces the general objective of the project in one sentence; states the level of impact and why (what is the major contribution/advance?); identifies the major score-driving factors; and explains how you balanced/combined/weighted the various criteria in the overall impact score. This paragraph is based on all individual pieces in the completed critique template and should make the impact level clear on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the specific aims are achieved, what would the project contribute to this field and how significant/important is this contribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance assumes success of the specific aims. Consider Rigor of Prior Research: is the prior research that provides the justification for the research objective rigorous? Focus on the importance of the proposed work in the field, NOT the importance of the disease/condition being studied. Direct relevance to human health is not required; significance can be basic/mechanistic, technological, translational, clinical, or public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the investigative team have the collective expertise to lead the project, do the work, and interpret the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess evidence of appropriate expertise for the proposed project and evidence of, or potential for, successful project management and execution. Investigator independence should not be considered. For Multi-PI (MPI) applications, address each Principal Investigator and the Leadership Plan. For Multi-Center Clinical Trials, address the organizational structure and investigators for the coordinating center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge or seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms? Are novel concepts/approaches/methods/instrumentation/interventions employed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the level of 'out-of-the-box' thinking (new directions, unique approaches, or novel use of existing methods across fields). Do not feel obligated to find innovation if it is not present. Innovation need not be a driver of impact; you can assign a weak innovation score and still assign a strong Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the strategy, methods, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the big picture (rationale and study design) rather than minor details. Describe why you think an aspect is a strength or weakness. Evaluate whether the strategy is likely to produce unbiased and interpretable results and whether it addresses weaknesses in the rigor of prior research. Confirm the application appropriately accounts for sex and relevant biological variables. For Clinical Trials, comment on adequate power, appropriate study population, ethical issues, methods to assess effects of intervention, and quality control. Avoid simply restating aims. Taking risks is acceptable. Prioritize and label concerns as major (score-driving) or minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the resources, facilities, and equipment appropriate for the needs of the proposed project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should NOT be an assessment of institutional prestige or overall quality. Think about what environment/resources are necessary for the project's success and evaluate the institution's ability to provide those conditions and support. For Clinical Trials, consider capabilities of all sites/centers for data coordination, enrollment, laboratory testing, and conducting the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline (if Clinical Trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the proposed study timeline for feasibility and justification when a Clinical Trial is part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be filled in if a Clinical Trial is part of the application. Add comments regarding details, feasibility, and justification of the proposed timeline, whether the study incorporates efficiencies, utilizes existing resources, and discusses potential challenges and solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: If human subjects are involved (and not exempt), comment on protections and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must provide comments on whether the following four points are appropriately addressed: (1) the risk to subjects; (2) the adequacy of protections against risk; (3) potential benefits of the research to subjects and others; and (4) the importance of the knowledge to be gained. If the application proposes a clinical trial, also comment on whether the applicants provided an acceptable Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and/or Data Safety Monitoring Board, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Age Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion by sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed plans for inclusion of individuals on the basis of sex or gender, race, ethnicity, and age. For NIH-defined Phase III clinical trials, comment on whether the study can be expected to identify potential differences by sex/gender, race, and/or ethnicity and whether plans for valid design and analysis of potential group differences are adequate for the scientific goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: If research involves live vertebrate animals, comment on key animal-care and use considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comments on whether the following are appropriately addressed: (1) description of procedures; (2) justification for choice of species; (3) minimization of pain and distress; and (4) justification for euthanasia method (only if not consistent with AVMA guidelines). For additional guidance see the Reviewer Training Module for the Vertebrate Animals Section and VAS Reviewer Cheat Sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on plans to handle biohazards and adequacy of protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications do not contain a separate Biohazards section; biohazards can be addressed throughout the application (including Facilities). Provide comments on plans for proper handling procedures and that adequate protections are addressed (personnel training, safety protocols, containment facilities, waste disposal). See Guidance for Review of Biohazards including Select Agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Transparency (research practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include attention to rigor of prior research, scientific rigor, consideration of biological variables, and authentication of resources as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address rigor and transparency where appropriate: rigor of prior research supporting objectives, scientific rigor of proposed work, consideration of biological variables including sex, and biological/chemical resource authentication (plans to identify/regularly validate key resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the applicant provided an appropriate plan for identifying and regularly validating key biological/chemical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on adequacy of resource authentication plans (regular validation, identification of key reagents/resources). See related guidance referenced in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether projects to be conducted in foreign organizations present special opportunities/resources not readily available in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Did the application appropriately explain/justify how the project in the foreign organization presents special opportunities or resources not readily available in the United States? Note: this review criterion does not apply to U.S. organizations containing a foreign component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Address review considerations for research involving select agents/biohazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Guidance for Review of Biohazards including Select Agents for specific evaluation criteria and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether resource sharing plans comply with expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidance for Review of Resource Sharing Plans. Comment as appropriate on the adequacy of proposed resource sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the budget and requested period of support are appropriate for the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidance for Review of Budget. Comment on whether the budget and period of support are reasonable and justified for the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions, Renewals, and Revisions (administrative comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a resubmission, renewal, or revision, add comments in the appropriate box indicating how the application has changed or been addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill out Resubmissions if the grant number ends in 'A1'; Renewals if the grant number starts with a '2'; Revisions if the grant number starts with a '3' (rare). Add comments in the appropriate section for these application types.
